plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.
Add to income ETF (QQQI) to 15% for stability.
Buy Gold (GLD) for diversification.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a larger cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower monthly gains around 1.5% by significantly reducing leverage and focusing on stability. The risk of large drawdowns is minimized, but so is the potential for rapid growth.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to small positions.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 25% to address concentration.
Buy Gold (GLD) for diversification.
Add to strong AI/Software name (CRWD) to 10%.
This plan balances risk reduction with continued growth potential.
balanced.read: This balanced strategy targets approximately 2.5% monthly gains by reducing leverage and concentration while adding some defensive assets. It aims for steady growth with controlled risk, avoiding extreme drawdowns.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.
Buy Gold (GLD) for diversification.
Add new high-scoring tech names (NET, CRDO) to 8% each.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for maximum growth.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly gains by increasing leverage and concentrating on high-scoring setups, including leveraged ETFs. Expect significantly higher potential upside but also much larger drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses, especially with leveraged ETF decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Significantly increase income ETF (QQQI) to 30%.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 20% to reduce concentration.
Buy Gold (GLD) for diversification.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and capital preservation.
income.read: This income-focused strategy aims for approximately 1% monthly gains through distributions, prioritizing stability and cash flow. Leverage and high-beta single names are cut to near zero, minimizing drawdown risk but also limiting growth potential.
